title: Jesus and Nicodemus, John the Baptist Exalts Christ

questions.question: Who was Nicodemus?
options: A Pharisee, a ruler of the Jews
A Roman centurion residing in Jerusalem
A tax collector from Jericho
A Sadducee high priest entirely
questions.correctAnswer: A Pharisee, a ruler of the Jews
questions.explanation: John 3:1 (ESV): "Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews."

questions.question: When did Nicodemus come to see Jesus?
options: By night
At the ninth hour
Early in the morning
During the midday heat
questions.explanation: John 3:2 (ESV): "This man came to Jesus by night"

questions.question: Jesus told Nicodemus, "Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born again he cannot..." what?
options: "...see the kingdom of God."
"...inherit the earth."
"...become a child of Abraham."
"...understand the prophets entirely."
questions.explanation: John 3:3 (ESV): "Jesus answered him, 'Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born again he cannot see the kingdom of God.'"

questions.question: "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have..."?
options: eternal life
abundance of riches
the power of angels completely
peace on earth instantly
questions.explanation: John 3:16 (ESV): "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life."

questions.question: What did John the Baptist say about his relationship to Jesus?
options: "He must increase, but I must decrease."
"I am his equal in the sight of the Lord completely."
"I must forge the path, and he will walk surely upon it."
"He will lead Israel, but I will baptize the nations."
questions.correctAnswer: "He must increase, but I must decrease."
questions.explanation: John 3:30 (ESV): "He must increase, but I must decrease."

questions.question: When Nicodemus asked how someone old could be born again, Jesus stated one must be born of what two things to enter the kingdom?
options: Born of water and the Spirit
Born of blood and fire
Born of truth and light entirely
Born of repentance and faith
questions.correctAnswer: Born of water and the Spirit
questions.explanation: John 3:5 (ESV): "Jesus answered, 'Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.'"

questions.question: Jesus said the wind blows where it wishes, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with whom?
options: Everyone who is born of the Spirit
The Son of God descending
The prophets sent by the Father entirely
The angels surveying the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Everyone who is born of the Spirit
questions.explanation: John 3:8 (ESV): "The wind blows where it wishes, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone who is born of the Spirit."

questions.question: What Old Testament parallel did Jesus use saying: "And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be..."?
options: "...lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life."
"...restored to his rightful throne."
"...brought before the judges to be struck down."
"...broken so the people might live completely."
questions.correctAnswer: "...lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life."
questions.explanation: John 3:14-15 (ESV): "And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life."

questions.question: Why did God send His Son into the world according to John 3:17?
options: Not to condemn the world, but in order that the world might be saved through him
To judge the nations that rejected the prophets
To establish a physical kingdom in Jerusalem rapidly
To destroy those who operate in darkness
questions.correctAnswer: Not to condemn the world, but in order that the world might be saved through him
questions.explanation: John 3:17 (ESV): "For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but in order that the world might be saved through him."

questions.question: What is the judgment according to John 3:19? The light has come into the world, but people loved what rather than the light?
options: The darkness, because their works were evil
The riches of life safely contained
The traditions of their fathers entirely
The comfort of the Roman rule entirely
questions.correctAnswer: The darkness, because their works were evil
questions.explanation: John 3:19 (ESV): "And this is the judgment: the light has come into the world, and people loved the darkness rather than the light because their works were evil."

questions.question: How did Jesus challenge Nicodemus' status as the "teacher of Israel" for not understanding these things?
options: "We speak of what we know, and bear witness to what we have seen, but you do not receive our testimony."
"You know only the letters entirely, not the Spirit that gives life."
"You teach traditions of men while ignoring the laws of heaven."
"You seek signs when faith is what is required completely."
questions.correctAnswer: "We speak of what we know, and bear witness to what we have seen, but you do not receive our testimony."
questions.explanation: John 3:11 (ESV): "Truly, truly, I say to you, we speak of what we know, and bear witness to what we have seen, but you do not receive our testimony."

questions.question: Why does everyone who does wicked things hate the light and not come to the light?
options: Lest his works should be exposed
Because it blinds the eyes accustomed to the dark
Lest he be judged immediately by angels
Because the light demands sacrifice and blood entirely
questions.correctAnswer: Lest his works should be exposed
questions.explanation: John 3:20 (ESV): "For everyone who does wicked things hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his works should be exposed."

questions.question: How did John the Baptist describe his own joy when comparing Jesus to the bridegroom?
options: "The friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice. Therefore this joy of mine is now complete."
"The servant rejoices when the master finds his bride securely."
"The herald shouts for joy as the wedding begins entirely."
"The best man must step aside in silence while the feast starts."
questions.correctAnswer: "The friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice. Therefore this joy of mine is now complete."
questions.explanation: John 3:29 (ESV): "The one who has the bride is the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice. Therefore this joy of mine is now complete."

questions.question: John stated "For he whom God has sent utters the words of God, for he gives the Spirit..." how?
options: "...without measure."
"...drop by drop like precious rain."
"...only to those who are worthy completely."
"...to shatter the darkness fully."
questions.explanation: John 3:34 (ESV): "For he whom God has sent utters the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure."

questions.question: The final verse of chapter 3 says: "Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; whoever does not obey the Son shall not see life..." but what remains on him?
options: "...but the wrath of God remains on him."
"...but eternal darkness waits for him completely."
"...but he shall be broken in the judgment."
"...but his soul is cast out forever entirely."
questions.correctAnswer: "...but the wrath of God remains on him."
questions.explanation: John 3:36 (ESV): "Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; whoever does not obey the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God remains on him."

key_verse_text: "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life."
